subject: History
description: Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Vidyasagar, Phule, Ambedkar

questions.stem: The founder of the Brahmo Samaj (1828), who campaigned against Sati, was:
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (1772-1833) — often called the 'Father of Modern India'/'Father of the Indian Renaissance' — founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828 (renamed Brahmo Samaj). His campaigning led to Lord William Bentinck's 1829 Regulation abolishing Sati. He died in Bristol, England. Vidyasagar led the widow-remarriage campaign. Dayananda Saraswati founded Arya Samaj in 1875. Vivekananda spoke at the Parliament of the World's Religions, Chicago, 1893.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Widow Remarriage Act, 1856, was the direct result of the untiring efforts of:
questions.explanation: Vidyasagar (1820-91) — scholar, educator, polymath — petitioned the government with supporting scriptural evidence; the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act 1856 followed. He also promoted girls' education and founded the Metropolitan Institution (now Vidyasagar College). Ram Mohan Roy had earlier focused on Sati abolition (1829). Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj. Ranade co-founded the Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra (1867).

questions.stem: Jyotirao Phule and his wife Savitribai Phule are most celebrated for their work on:

options.option_text: Women's education and rights of lower castes

questions.explanation: Jyotirao Phule (1827-90) — with his wife Savitribai Phule (1831-97) — founded India's first school for girls in Pune in 1848. He formed the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873) to oppose caste and promote the rights of Shudras and untouchables. His book 'Gulamgiri' (1873) analyses caste oppression and is dedicated to the abolition of slavery in the US. Savitribai is regarded as India's first woman teacher.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The 'Arya Samaj' was founded in 1875 by:
questions.explanation: Dayananda Saraswati (1824-83) — founded Arya Samaj at Bombay in 1875 with the motto 'Back to the Vedas'. He opposed idolatry, polytheism, caste hierarchy and child marriage; supported Shuddhi (reconversion) and widow remarriage. His Satyartha Prakash ('Light of Truth') is the key text. Keshub Chandra Sen led a breakaway Brahmo Samaj of India after 1866. Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.

questions.stem: Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired which important committee of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: Dr B. R. Ambedkar (1891-1956) chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly (appointed 29 Aug 1947). He is widely considered the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'. Earlier work — the Hindu Code Bill (which he resigned over), the Mahad Satyagraha (1927), the Kalaram Temple entry (1930). He embraced Buddhism along with thousands of followers on 14 October 1956. Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1990.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Swami Vivekananda's famous speech at the Parliament of the World's Religions was delivered in 1893 at:
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda (1863-1902) addressed the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago on 11 September 1893 with the famous 'Sisters and Brothers of America' opening. The Art Institute of Chicago has a plaque in his honour. His birth anniversary (12 January) is observed as National Youth Day in India. He founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897).

questions.stem: Sati (the practice of a widow being burned on her husband's funeral pyre) was legally abolished in British India by a Regulation passed in 1829 by Governor-General:
questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck (Governor-General 1828-35) passed Regulation XVII of 1829 declaring Sati illegal in the Bengal Presidency; it was extended to Madras and Bombay in 1830. The Regulation followed a long campaign by Raja Ram Mohan Roy. Other Bentinck reforms — use of English as medium of instruction (1835, on Macaulay's Minute), suppression of the Thugs. Lord Dalhousie annexed states via the Doctrine of Lapse; Lord Ripon introduced local self-government (1882).
